study type: Pooled analysis of three cohorts (retrospective cohort, randomized trial, prospective cohort)
cohort: The study included 530 women aged 18-40 years, heterosexually active, without known subfertility, and not taking exogenous hormones.
finding: Sexual intercourse was associated with longer cycles, longer luteal phases, a lower probability of luteal phase deficiency, a lower probability of premenstrual spotting, and a higher probability of having more days of peak-type (estrogenic) cervical fluid.
